paper.title: Transcriptome analysis of genes and metabolic pathways associated with nicotine degradation in Aspergillus oryzae 112822
paper.authors: He C, Huang Y, Liu P, Wei J, Yang Y, Xu L, Xiao M.
paper.association_evidence: Availability of data: 'retrieved under the accession number SRP156238'; SRP156238 is the study accession (ENA secondary id) of PRJNA484246.

study_summary.objective: Identify the genes and pathways that let the tobacco-leaf isolate A. oryzae 112822 tolerate and degrade nicotine.
study_summary.experimental_design: Mycelia were grown 20 h in rich medium, then moved to a dextrose medium (control, YD) or a nicotine medium (Nic) for 16 h at 28 C; three biological replicates each, sequenced on HiSeq 4000.
study_summary.main_finding: Nicotine changed 4,381 genes (2,291 up, 2,090 down), including cytochrome P450 and oxidase candidates for nicotine demethylation, antioxidant enzymes and glutathione S-transferases.

a112822_flask.note: 2 g/L yeast extract in both media
after transfer to the test medium

nicotine_exposure.note: 2 g/L nicotine in place of dextrose
nicotine led to overproduction of reactive oxygen species

notes: The nicotine medium contains no dextrose, so the carbon source changes together with the nicotine exposure.
Resting cells from the nicotine medium degraded 83% of added nicotine in 48 h, while cells from the dextrose medium did not (paper, Fig. 1).
